title: Deployment Window Scheduler and Interlock Exchange
creator: Priya Singh
description: Create a lightweight Deployment Window Scheduler service (DWS) and an Interlock Exchange protocol to coordinate regional deployment windows, cross-team handoffs, and rollback triggers for runtime/console/API surface launches. The goal is to reduce deployment conflicts, clarify ownership for cutovers, and provide machine-readable windows that CI/CD and oncall tooling can consume.
acceptance_criteria: DWS exposes an API for teams to request, reserve, and release deployment windows with metadata (region, service, allowed concurrency, blackout flags)
Interlock Exchange can be called by CI to verify a window before starting a deploy and returns deterministic allow/deny with reason codes
Console shows a read-only calendar view of scheduled windows and active reservations filtered by team and region
Runbook auto-notifications created when overlapping requests are made and policy-based escalation is triggered
Integration tests validate CI gating with a mocked Interlock Exchange and show rollback triggers firing on policy violations
updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Console, and CI teams. Agreed scope: API + calendar view + CI gate. Action: ENG to prototype API contract.
2025-02-18: ENG API contract v0.1 reviewed. PM feedback to add ‘concurrency_hint’ and ‘sla_bucket’ fields for capacity hedging.
2025-02-25: Design provided initial calendar wireframes emphasizing filter by service and region. Console team requests compact week view for oncall.
2025-03-03: Security requested data retention clarifications; PM scoped to keep reservation audit for 180 days. Decided no sensitive payloads stored.
2025-03-05: Product review with Director approved project as Planned. Estimate set to 8 points; target kickoff in Cycle 2025-W10.
decisions: Use a simple REST contract for Interlock Exchange (POST /v1/check) to return allow/deny with standardized reason codes
Expose read-only calendar in Console rather than full write flows to minimize migration work for teams initially
Retention window for reservation logs set to 180 days to balance auditability and storage cost
Policy engine will be rules-first (team/region/blackout) with scope to add ML-based conflict predictions in later phases
risks: Teams may bypass DWS and continue ad-hoc deployments if CI integration is not enforced; mitigation: introduce CI gates as part of developer templates and require in launch playbook
Incorrect window reservations could block urgent security fixes; mitigation: include emergency override flow with approval audit
Console calendar view could surface stale data if not cached correctly; mitigation: implement short TTL and explicit refresh controls for oncall users
notes: Trade-offs discussed: initial scope avoids full reservation editing from Console to reduce permission surface. This speeds delivery but defers self-serve UX.
Considered using existing scheduling service (ENG-11321) but opted for DWS to keep domain logic close to launches and allow lightweight iteration.
Evaluating capacity tagging (low/medium/high) to guide Dedicated capacity hedging versus hosted fallback lanes. Requires ENG metric inputs.
